statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The Asian-hours drift has been fully retraced. NQ trades near 29,130.25, up 24.50 points or 0.08% from the 29,105.75 settle, at the upper end of a 29,017.00-29,142.00 overnight range that spans 125 points, or 0.43%. An hour earlier the same contract sat near 29,025 at the low of that range, so the entire overnight decline has been recovered. Tokyo disagrees: the Nikkei 225 is near 64,940, down 0.90%, a third consecutive decline. Monday's US session closed with the Nasdaq Composite at 25,980.19, down 0.76%, and the S&P 500 at 7,652.86, down 0.28%, on a memory-led chip de-rating in which Micron fell 5.83%, Nvidia 2.91% and Broadcom 2.63%. VIX finished at 15.85, the 10-year yield sits near 4.71% and the 2-year near 4.25%, and WTI is around 85.28 after Monday's decline on the new Iran sanctions programme. Tail is 9 in the low band because a completed retracement is the direct opposite of the path this measure targets. Stress is 45 in the elevated band on the chip de-rating and the Core PCE, GDP revision and Nvidia stack that lands on Wednesday.
recommendation: Descriptive only. The defining observation is that a retracement occurred and completed: NQ recovered the full 113-point overnight decline and traded back above the prior settle within roughly one hour, while Asian cash indices remained lower. Mean reversion is functioning across the divergence rather than being denied. None of the amplifiers this measure requires is present - there is no gap, no repeated extension after failed pullbacks and no holding near a session extreme. Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON with a green status for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The flagged danger window spans 13:30Z-14:30Z, covering the US cash open and the 14:00Z Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and Richmond Fed cluster. Every forecast hour maps to EA_ON because the conditional Tail path peaks at 18, below the watch band. Confidence is 85: the futures level, range and settle are confirmed by two independent quote sources, with the Nikkei, yields, oil, VIX and the seven-day calendar verified from primary sources and two stale delayed-quote pages discarded.
headline: NQ retraces the entire overnight decline to 29,130.25, back above the 29,105.75 settle while Tokyo falls a third session, easing Tail to 9 with Stress at 45 ahead of Wednesday's Core PCE and Nvidia stack
body:
The evidence that matters this hour is a completed round trip. Around 00:30Z NQ was trading near 29,025 at the low of its overnight range; it now trades near 29,130.25, up 24.50 points or 0.08% against the 29,105.75 settle, at the upper end of a 29,017.00-29,142.00 band. That is a full recovery of a 113-point decline inside roughly one hour, confirmed independently by two quote sources. Holding near an overnight extreme is one of the amplifiers this measure watches for, but the extreme now being tested is the high, and it was reached by reverting from the low rather than by extending from it. A market that retraces its own overnight move in one hour is demonstrating exactly the behaviour whose absence would define the pathological path.

The regional backdrop is genuinely weaker, which makes the divergence informative rather than alarming. The Nikkei 225 sits near 64,940, down about 588 points or 0.90%, extending its decline to a third consecutive session on technology weakness and questions about AI infrastructure spending. Monday's US session had the same character: the Nasdaq Composite closed at 25,980.19, down 0.76%, and the S&P 500 at 7,652.86, down 0.28%, while the semiconductor complex closed with none of its seven tracked names higher. Micron fell 5.83% to 910.43 after Netlist filed new International Trade Commission and federal court patent cases covering DDR5 memory products, Advanced Micro Devices fell 3.49%, Intel 3.12%, Nvidia 2.91% and Broadcom 2.63%. Against that, five of the eight tracked megacaps closed higher - Meta 1.66%, Amazon 1.33%, Alphabet 0.94%, Microsoft 0.84% and Apple 0.32% - producing megacap dispersion above two points. A tape where the largest weights disagree with each other is a rotation, not a one-way index path, and the Nasdaq-100 accordingly held up better than the broader composite.

Cross-asset confirmation is mild in both directions. VIX finished Monday at 15.85, essentially unchanged, and overnight volatility futures are flat; that is not the signature of a market pricing a disorderly leg. The 10-year yield near 4.71% remains close to a 20-month high around 4.75%, and the 2-year near 4.25% keeps the front end firm, so rates are a persistent background pressure rather than a fresh shock. WTI trades around 85.28 after falling more than 2% on Monday, when the Treasury announced a new Iran sanctions programme targeting digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping alongside more than 60 designated entities and vessels. Oil falling on an escalation headline is itself evidence that the market is treating the announcement as a supply-neutral policy step rather than a transmission channel into equities. Gold firmed just under 1% overnight, a modest hedging bid rather than a flight.

The forward shape is dominated by scheduled events rather than observed structure. Tuesday carries a Fed Barkin speech at 12:00Z, the weekly ADP reading at 12:15Z, the 14:00Z cluster of Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and the Richmond Fed index, a 2-year note auction at 17:00Z and a second Barkin appearance at 20:00Z. Wednesday concentrates the real load: July Core PCE, the second estimate of second-quarter GDP and durable goods orders all at 12:30Z, with Nvidia's results after the cash close - a set that arrives with the chip complex already de-rated and with reports that Nvidia has notified customers of server price increases above 15% as memory costs climb. Jackson Hole then runs from Thursday through Saturday, with the Fed Chair's keynote scheduled Friday at 14:00Z. That stack is why Stress holds in the elevated band at 45 while Tail sits at 9. Under the calibration this system uses, scheduled importance and forecast dispersion belong to Stress and Confidence; Tail only follows once a price path is observed that denies retracement. The observation available this hour is the exact opposite.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. The window opened at 01:00Z on 24 August with Tail 7 and Stress 38 in a normal mode and held a 7-12 band through the Asian and early European hours. The first structural peak came at 07:00Z, where the European open produced Tail 19 and Stress 58 in a trend-down mode; it faded to 17 within an hour and to 12 by 09:00Z. The window's only non-green slots surrounded the US cash open: Tail 20 with Stress 54 in an event/whipsaw mode at 13:00Z mapped to WATCH, and the single peak at 14:00Z reached Tail 26 with Stress 60 in a trend-down mode, mapping to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. That structure did not persist. From 15:00Z onward Tail collapsed to 13 and then held a 7-10 band for the remainder of the US session while Stress decayed from 54 to 42, the signature of a rotation whose directional efficiency faded rather than a path that denied mean reversion. The window closed at 00:00Z on 25 August with Tail 12, Stress 45 and a mixed mode as futures drifted to the low of a narrow overnight range - a level that has since been fully recovered.
outlookSummary: The conditional path stays inside the low Tail band for all 24 hours, so every slot maps to EA_ON. It opens at 9 on the observed overnight round trip, holds a 9-10 band through the Asian session where the horizon floor of 10 coincides with the thinnest liquidity and the lowest conditional Stress of 43, then lifts to 13 at 07:00Z for the European open - the same window that produced Monday's first structural peak and then faded it. The series consolidates in an 11-12 band through the European morning and the 12:00Z Barkin and ADP checkpoints. The horizon peak of 18 falls at 14:00Z, where the first full US cash hour overlaps the Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and Richmond Fed cluster; that hour also carries the horizon's Stress peak of 55 and, together with 13:00Z, the only event/whipsaw modes in the forecast. Conditional Tail then decays to 13 by 16:00Z as post-data volatility normally fades, holds 12-13 through the 2-year auction and the closing rotation, and eases to 10 across the CME maintenance halt and the reopen. It settles at 11 into the Asian opens on the eve of Core PCE and Nvidia results, where conditional Stress firms to 48. No hour reaches the watch threshold of 20, because none of the amplifiers that would justify it has been observed rather than merely scheduled.

Tokyo is weaker, with the Nikkei 225 near 64,940, down 0.90%. Mean reversion is functioning, so Tail eases to 9.
